sentences.text:
Date of decision: 08.10.
 Ramesh @ Ramesh Devi ...Petitione
 Vs.
 Narender and others ...Responden
Coram: Hon'Ble Ms. Justice Nidhi Gupta

Present:- Mr. Sanjay Ghalawat, Advocate
 for the petitioner.

Mr. Sanjeev Kumar Birla, Advocate
 for respondents No. 1 and 2.

Mr. Mukesh Yadav, Advocate for
 respondents No. 4 to 8.
 ***
 Nidhi Gupta, J.
Present Civil Revision Petition has been filed by the claimant under Article 227 of the Constitution
of India for Setting aside the order dated 06.09.2023 (Annexure P-1) passed by Ld. Mact, Rewari;
whereby the Application of the Petitioner filed "under Section 10 of Cpc for staying the subsequent
proceeding arising out of Claim Petition bearing Macp No. 285 of 2021 titled as "Sandeep Kumar
versus Narender and Others" has been dismissed and the same is illegal, unreasonable and passed
in contravention of established principles of Section 10 of Cpc."

2.  It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that the learned Tribunal was in patent error in dismissing the application of the petitioner under Section 10 of CPC as it failed to appreciate the established legal position that the proceeding, which was filed prior in time, is to be treated as the main case.

It is submitted that in the present case, there can be no dispute with regard to the fact that the petitioner had filed her Claim Petition No. 126 of 2021 (District-Jhajjar) on 07.04.2021 (Annexure P-2) in which notice was issued by the learned Tribunal vide order dated 08.04.2021 (Annexure P-3).
Whereas respondent No.4 had filed her Claim Petition bearing MACP No. 285 of 2021 (District-Rewari) on 07.07.2021 (Annexure P-4) in which notice was issued vide order dated 08.07.2021 (Annexure P-5).

It is submitted that accordingly, petitioner had filed an application dated 16.03.2023 under Section 10 CPC (Annexure P-12); thereby praying that the MACP No. 285 of 2021 (District-Rewari) filed by respondent No.4 and her children be stayed.

However, vide the impugned order dated 06.09.2023 (Annexure P-1), the said application of the petitioner has been Ramesh vs Naredner And Others on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100714754/
1 dismissed.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel contends that if the conditions of 10 CPC are satisfied then the subsequent suit/claim is liable to be stayed as the issue involved in both the proceedings are directly and substantially same in the subsequent suit/claim as to the previous suit and, therefore, decision in the previous suit/claim will operate as res judicata for the purpose of deciding subsequent suit/claim.

In the present case as the MACP Case No. 285 of 2021 (District-Rewari) was filed by respondent No.4 after filing of MACP Case No. 126 of 2021 (District-Jhajjar) filed by the petitioner,
the same was liable to be stayed.
However, the learned Tribunal has failed to appreciate this fact of the matter.
Therefore, the impugned order dated 06.09.2023 (Annexure P-1) deserves to be set aside.
4. Learned counsel for the respondents submit that the impugned order suffers from no error and accordingly pray for dismissal of the present Civil Revision Petition.
5. No other argument is raised on behalf of the parties.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case file in detail.

7. Perusal of the record of the case shows that the petitioner had filed MACP No. 126 of 2021 (District-Jhajjar) dated 07.04.2021 (Annexure P-2) on behalf of her injured son-Sandeep Kumar,
who had suffered injuries in accident dated 23.12.2020 and who was in Coma, for grant of compensation of Rs.1 Crore under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as "the Act") before the learned MACT, Jhajjar.

Simultaneously, the wife and minor children of Sandeep Kumar/respondents No. 4 to 8 herein, had also filed a Claim Petition bearing MACP No.
285 of 2021 (District-Rewari) dated 07.07.2021 (Annexure P-4) seeking grant of compensation of Rs.70 lacs under Section 166 of the Act before the MACT, Rewari.
During the pendency of these claim petitions, Sandeep Kumar had expired on 18.07.2022.

Subsequently, both the Claim Petitions were amended i.e. the petitioner amended her present Claim Petition bearing MACP No. 126 of 2021 (District-Jhajjar) for impleading respondent No.4 and her minor children as party respondents therein.

Similarly, respondents No. 4 to 8 also amended MACP No. 285 of 2021 (District-Rewari);
thereby impleading the present petitioner as party respondent therein.

8. The case file reveals that petitioner had also filed an application dated 16.03.2023 (Annexure P-12) under Section 10 CPC before the MACT, Rewari seeking stay of the MACP No. 285 of 2021 (District-Rewari).
It is the case of the petitioner that vide the impugned order dated 06.09.2023 (Annexure P-1), the said application of the petitioner has been dismissed by the MACT, Rewari.
However, a perusal of the impugned order dated 6.9.2023 reveals that application filed by the petitioner under Order 1 Rule 10 CPC has been dismissed.
The impugned order reads as follows: -

"Learned counsel for applicant Smt. Ramesh Devi submitted that claim petition No.MACP-126-2021 titled as Sandeep Vs. Narender Singh etc. is pending in the court of Sh. Fakhruddin, MACT, Jhajjar for 27.09.2023.
Petitioner after death of Sandeep made his wife and children as proforma respondents on 03.11.2022.

2

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for petitioner non applicant submitted that after death of Sandeep Kumar on 18.07.2022 the petitioners were impleaded as proforma respondents in claim petition No.126-2021 titled as Sandeep Vs. Narender and Others.
Petitioners i.e. wife and minor children have filed claim petition by impleading Smt. Ramesh Devi as proforma respondent on 08.07.2022.
Therefore, application may be dismissed.

From examination of record in light of aforesaid rival contentions, it is crystal clear that claim petition No.126-2021 titled as Sandeep Vs. Narender and Others was regarding injuries sustained in accident through is mother Smt. Ramesh Devi.
Claim petition No.285-2021 titled as Sandeep Kumar Vs. Narender and Others is through his wife was filed for injuries on 08.07.2022.

entities.text: Sandeep Kumar Vs. Narender and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
After death of Sandeep on 18.07.2022,
petitioners have impleaded Smt. Ramesh Devi as proforma respondent.
Petitioners mentioned in this claim petition have been impleaded as proforma respondents in claim petition No.126-2021 titled as Sandeep Vs. Narender and Others on 03.11.2022.
In view of material fact of impleading of proforma respondent No.4 before impleading of petitioners, the application dated 17.03.2023 under Order 1 Rule 10 CPC is dismissed.
As requested, case is adjourned to 09.09.2023 for settlement in National Lok Adalat."
9. Thus, there is no mention anywhere in the impugned order regarding any application filed by the petitioner under Section 10 CPC.

Even in the prayer clause of the present revision petition,
petitioner has sought setting aside of the order dated 06.09.2023 (Annexure P-1); thereby dismissing the application of the petitioner under Section 10 CPC; whereas order dated 06.09.2023 (Annexure P-1) is passed dismissing application of the petitioner under Order 1 Rule 10 CPC.
During arguments, it has been contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that in actual fact,

application of the petitioner under Section 10 CPC has been dismissed vide the said order dated 06.09.2023 (Annexure P-1); and a typographical error has been made in the impugned order wherein it is wrongly mentioned that application under Order 1 Rule 10 CPC had been dismissed.

However, on a Court query, it is admitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that no application was filed by the petitioner before the MACT, Rewari for correction of the said alleged typographical error.
Thus, even if there was a typographical error, petitioner has failed to file an appropriate application as per law, for correction before the Tribunal.
10. Moreover, the case file further reveals another discrepancy.

Annexure P-12 is an application filed by the petitioner under Section 10 CPC in MACP Case No. 285 of 2021 titled as "Sandeep Vs.
Narender Singh Etc."; whereas impugned order dated 06.09.2023 (Annexure P-1) is passed in MACP Case No. 546 of 2021 titled as "Yudhister vs. Narender and Others".

Thus, even names of the Ramesh vs Naredner And Others on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100714754/
3 parties do not tally.
Ld. counsel for the petitioner is unable to explain this discrepancy.
11. Thus, the present Civil Revision Petition stands dismissed.
However, liberty is granted to the petitioner to take recourse to appropriate remedy as per law, if any, and if so advised.
12. Pending application(s), if any, also stand(s) disposed of.
Divyanshi JUDGE
